differential.name: Resistant hypertension (pseudo‑resistant due to suboptimal therapy) driven by obesity‑related metabolic syndrome

supporting_evidence.finding: Stage‑2 hypertension (DBP 107 mmHg) despite ACE‑inhibitor therapy
Reviewer notes suboptimal regimen (no thiazide/CCB) suggesting pseudo‑resistance

differential.reasoning: Elevated BP persists despite ACE‑inhibitor; obesity and metabolic syndrome are potent contributors. Lack of a full three‑drug regimen makes true resistance uncertain, favoring a pseudo‑resistant classification.

differential.name: Obesity‑related metabolic syndrome

supporting_evidence.finding: High 10‑year ASCVD risk driven by hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes

differential.reasoning: Obesity drives insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and volume expansion, amplifying hypertension and cardiovascular risk.

differential.name: Chronic kidney disease, hypertensive nephrosclerosis (stage 3a)

supporting_evidence.finding: Elevated serum creatinine with no eGFR reported (suggesting reduced renal function)

differential.reasoning: Chronic hypertension can cause nephrosclerosis; reduced renal function may also perpetuate hypertension.

differential.name: Renal artery stenosis

supporting_evidence.finding: Reviewer flagged missing renal‑artery imaging; high pre‑test probability in obese, hypertensive patient
Resistant‑type hypertension with possible secondary cause

differential.reasoning: Renal artery stenosis is a treatable secondary cause of resistant hypertension, especially in patients with atherosclerotic risk factors.

differential.name: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)

supporting_evidence.finding: High prevalence of OSA in obese, hypertensive patients; no sleep study performed

differential.reasoning: OSA can cause sympathetic overactivity and worsen hypertension; screening is warranted.

differential.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn’s syndrome)

supporting_evidence.finding: Reviewer notes lack of aldosterone‑renin testing; still plausible in resistant hypertension cohort

differential.reasoning: Although not yet screened, primary aldosteronism remains a possible contributor to resistant hypertension.

differential.name: Anemia of chronic disease / iron‑deficiency anemia

supporting_evidence.finding: Discordant hemoglobin (17.4 g/dL) and hematocrit (36 %) values; anemia noted but data unreliable

differential.reasoning: Laboratory inconsistencies limit confidence; anemia may be a lab artifact or mild chronic disease.

primary_diagnosis: Resistant hypertension (pseudo‑resistant due to suboptimal therapy) driven by obesity‑related metabolic syndrome
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s uncontrolled stage‑2 hypertension persists despite ACE‑inhibitor therapy and is strongly linked to obesity and metabolic syndrome. Suboptimal antihypertensive regimen suggests pseudo‑resistance rather than true resistant hypertension. Obesity, CKD, and possible secondary causes (renal artery stenosis, OSA, primary aldosteronism) contribute variably. Anemia and metabolic acidosis remain unexplained and warrant further work‑up.
unresolved_findings: Missing numeric BMI value (obesity inferred only)
No calculated eGFR or urine albumin‑creatinine ratio
Incomplete iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation, TIBC)
Absent aldosterone‑renin ratio and plasma aldosterone measurement
No renal‑artery imaging (CTA/MRA or duplex ultrasound)
No mental‑health screening (PHQ‑9, GAD‑7) despite psychosocial stressors
Non‑anion‑gap metabolic acidosis without dedicated diagnosis
Absent documentation of smoking, alcohol use, and family history
recommended_workup: Repeat CBC with differential and verify hemoglobin/hematocrit values
Iron studies: ferritin, transferrin saturation, TIBC
Comprehensive metabolic panel with arterial blood gas to characterize metabolic acidosis
Calculate eGFR and obtain urine albumin‑creatinine ratio
Polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing
Aldosterone‑renin ratio with confirmatory saline infusion test if indicated
Renal artery duplex ultrasound; consider CTA/MRA if duplex equivocal
24‑hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to confirm true resistance
Medication adherence assessment and optimization of regimen (add thiazide‑type diuretic and/or calcium‑channel blocker)
Mental‑health screening (PHQ‑9, GAD‑7) and social support evaluation
Detailed social history: smoking, alcohol, family cardiovascular disease
